title: Building my first 2D game with AI — am I missing any essential tools?
author: Bright_Lecture_1137
selftext:
I'm a beginner and planning to make my first 2D game for Android/PC. I can handle the creative/design side (characters, backgrounds, weapons, etc.), but I'm very inexperienced with coding, so I'm planning to use an AI coding agent heavily for the programming.

My current setup/tools:

Godot 4.x — game engine

VS Code — development

Git + GitHub — version control/backups

Krita — 2D art/characters/backgrounds

Audacity — audio editing

LMMS — music

Free AI coding agent — still deciding between things like Copilot/Freebuff/Roo/Cline/etc.

NVIDIA hosted AI APIs — also looking into these for coding/AI assistance

My goal is to keep the development cost at $0, at least while I'm learning/prototyping.

I'm mainly looking for an AI agent that can actually work on a Godot project — create/edit scripts, work across multiple files, help debug errors, run commands/tests, etc., rather than just autocomplete code.

I'm not going to describe the whole game yet, but it will be a 2D action-focused game with physics/combat and fairly detailed atmospheric environments.

Am I missing any important tools/workflows that I should set up before starting?

Also, if there are better free AI coding agents or free/large-limit AI APIs than the ones I mentioned, I'd really appreciate recommendations based on actual experience.

Hardware isn't an issue for running Godot, but I'd prefer cloud AI over local LLMs because I want better coding performance and don't want to be limited by my laptop's hardware.

Thanks 

My laptop specs are btw ( i5 hx processor, rtx 3050 6gb vram, 16 gb ram.)

comments.author: Short_Stable2397
comments.body:
Since you're using Godot and want your AI agent to help debugging errors, I have a free version of the Godot MCP I built that allows your agent to boot up Godot and inspect the game. More information at [GDMaestro website](https://asymptopia.dev/gdmaestro/) and I also have some comparison videos with and without the MCP on my profile.

As for the agent, I would recommend GLM 5.3 Flash and this weekend they're giving away 300M tokens, as well as off-peak (Singapore time) unlimited tokens until 20th September. Although you do have to pay at least the cheapest sub. Personally I use it for game dev more than Claude as I can iterate much more with all the free tokens and the differences really show up on the iterations than one shots.

replies.author: Bright_Lecture_1137
replies.body: Oh shit, thank you! The Godot MCP sounds especially interesting since I'm a complete beginner with coding. Being able to have the agent actually boot/inspect the game sounds insanely useful. I'll definitely check out GDMaestro. And GLM 5.3 Flash sounds interesting too i 'll look into the token offer. Appreciate the recommendation!

replies.author: Short_Stable2397
replies.body: You're welcome. Appreciate you checking it out. Hit me up if you have any questions.

replies.author: Bright_Lecture_1137
replies.body: Ahh okay 😂 Since I'm completely new to music production, would you personally go with LMMS or Audacity 4.0 for making simple game music/SFX? I don't really know the difference yet 😭

replies.author: Bluetails_Buizel
replies.body:
Why not both? And yes!

Also, try bandlabs/ GarageBand (iOS/macos) as they are very easy to make your own notes / melody.

But since music making is still new to you, I suggest looking up YouTube (Spotify/ soundcloud/ etc. works to, but eeh, I don’t have Spotify account) and see what kind of music that you like and actually would fit into your game. Paste the music here and I’ll let you know where to go from here.

replies.author: UnfortunateHurricane
replies.body: LMMS will take you months full-time to get something usable. Reaper+Vital is another DAC + synth combo I picked up when I thought I should do everything. But that is completely delusional. Your PC is not beefy enough but Acestep 1.5 xl is what I am using for music and good enough for me.

comments.author: UnfortunateHurricane
comments.body:
If you have absolutely no coding experience I would not advise trying to have those free agents write all the game code. If you are a US student you can get 4 months for free.

https://chatgpt.com/students/2026/

And even if not get the plus subscription. Those 20 dollars go along way. And save you all the pain of those basically useless ones.
GPT-Image is included and pretty amazing too

You might also want to use a vector graphics program like Inkscape. Or the weird combined one Affinity. Both free
